Passed/agreed to in House: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 417 - 7 (Roll no. 302). (text: CR H5605)

At the conclusion of debate, the Yeas and Nays were demanded and ordered. Pursuant to the provisions of clause 8, rule XX, the Chair announced that further proceedings on the motion would be postponed.

Considered under suspension of the rules. (consideration: CR H5605-5608)

dimensions.assessment: Directly affects specified federal financial agencies and indirectly impacts supervised financial institutions through future technology and reporting changes.
dimensions.evidence: Each covered agency shall... assess how existing technologies used by the covered agency pose challenges

dimensions.assessment: Primarily requires internal agency assessments, reviews of procurement protocols, and periodic reports to Congress.
dimensions.evidence: assess the procurement rules and protocols adhered to by such covered agency when such covered agency acquires or develops new technological systems

dimensions.assessment: Requires reporting and administrative reviews across agencies without stating specific new federal funding allocations or spending amounts.
Applies across numerous major financial regulatory agencies, requiring coordinated reporting and comprehensive internal reviews.
dimensions.evidence: the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, the Department of the Treasury... and the National Credit Union Administration

dimensions.assessment: Mandates ongoing reporting requirements occurring every five years following an initial assessment and report.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 18 months after the completion of the assessments required under subsection (a), and for every 5 years thereafter, the covered agencies shall coordinate and jointly submit

missing_information: Cost estimates for agencies to upgrade their supervisory technologies
Transition costs for regulated entities to adapt to future reporting changes
importance_detail.rationale: The bill requires multiple federal financial regulatory agencies to assess their internal technological capabilities, procurement rules, and data-sharing practices, and to report to Congress every five years. The primary effect is internal administrative evaluation and reporting rather than direct regulation of the public.
